title: Procureur général detains First President of the Cour de Cassation in Fonds souverain inquiry
content: The procureur général of the United Republics ordered the detention of Élisabeth Vaugelas, First President of the Cour de Cassation, shortly after six o’clock on Wednesday morning, plunging the country’s highest judicial institution and the government into an emergency *séance* and raising the prospect of a constitutional crisis.

According to a communiqué issued by the Parquet général, the measure concerns the alleged transmission of sealed documents to a member of the Conseil des ministres and the suppression of a *référé* that would have frozen two tranches of the Fonds souverain des Républiques (FSR), the state investment vehicle that manages roughly 480 billion livres.
img::/gazette/images/1/judge-get-caught.webp::Le palais de justice d’Aurelle, mercredi matin : la première présidente quitte le bâtiment sous escorte. Photographie : Agence des Républiques (ADR).

The Conseil supérieur de la magistrature met in an extraordinary session within the hour. In a statement, the syndicats de magistrats described the detention as “an unprecedented rupture of the separation of powers” and called on the President of the United Republics to intervene. The <u>garde des Sceaux</u>, Anne-Claire Delorme, declined to comment before a scheduled *interpellation* in the Assemblée des Républiques this afternoon.

The Assembly suspended its agenda at eight o’clock. The leader of the opposition bloc said a motion de *censure* would be tabled if the government failed to explain the sequence of events by Friday, while the commission des finances summoned the governor of the Banque des Républiques for a closed hearing.

Financial markets reacted immediately. The Indice d’Aurelle fell **2.8 per cent** at the open before recovering part of the loss, and the livre weakened 0.6 per cent against the reference basket. Traders said the immediate concern was not the fate of the fund but the credibility of the institutions that oversee it.

President Casimir Vaux returned early from a state visit to Marbre and convened the Conseil des ministres for this evening. A spokesman said the presidency would “respect the independence of the judiciary while ensuring the continuity of the state”, a formula that legal scholars said left the government’s position deliberately open.

The inquiry dates from June, when auditors first alerted the Parquet général to discrepancies in the fund’s quarterly reporting. Vaugelas, who has led the Cour de Cassation since 2021, denies any wrongdoing through her counsel and has asked to be heard in open court on Friday. The Parquet général has invoked the secret de l’instruction, leaving several central questions unanswered.
author: Hélène Vasseur, correspondante judiciaire — Agence des Républiques (ADR)
